name: architecture-east
estimated: some heights, with a photograph as a reference; the storeys' height, and on each floor of the main block's north-west faces a louvred parapet and a band of windows, and round the wing a band of windows; the face in dark cladding under the main block's north-west eave and the dormers out of it; and the faces no photograph shows, drawn plainly or after the ones it shows
refs_note: the folder of refs/ that holds the reference views (views.json, masks/), which refine, compare, metrics, sky_mask and the viewer's ?sv= read: refs/photos (gitignored), whose views tools/photo_camera.py writes. Its one photograph is taken from the raised terrace to the building's north-west, about 50 m from its tall tower, through a lens of about 53 degrees across; its camera is fitted to the two towers' top edges and three of their corners, with the principal point at the centre.

building.title: Architecture - East (421E), University of Auckland
building.note: outline: building 421E's outer ring from the main project's campus.json, in the map's frame; it chooses the crop box and the building's own points (frame.near_outline, measure and topview). The site replaces block 421E by its id.

origin.note: the campus origin, as in campus.json; the landmark's local metres = NZTM (EPSG:2193) minus the NZTM of this point, with grid north

door.note: the entrance is not known (the campus map records no lobby or entrance in 421E, and no street passes it: OpenStreetMap has only footways, steps and a service lane round it, with the Grafton Gully motorway to the east), so the door is on the raised terrace before the main block's north-west face, which the photograph shows people coming to, in the middle of the stretch where the terrace meets the face (u 9 to 37.5 in frame E), 2.5 m out from it (u 23, w 7). The LiDAR's ground within 1 m: 13 returns, p10/p50/p90 39.534/39.558/39.578 m; along the face the terrace lies at 39.56 to 40.01 m (p50 per 3 m, w 5 to 12)

frame.method: LiDAR building points (class 6) more than min_above m above the ground and within near_outline m of building.outline
frame.thresholds_note: min_above, tower_above and spine_below were 3, 3 and 40 m above the provisional ground (31.6 m); lowered by 7.96 m with the ground set at the door, so that they pick the same points and the measured frame stays the expected one

ground_note: the LiDAR's ground at the door (step 7, 2026-11-07); the provisional ground was 31.6 m, the median LiDAR ground in the crop box, from which the heights in parts/common.js are measured (its H moves them on to this ground)

light.note: estimated: the photograph is taken on a clear afternoon with the sun to the north-west, behind the camera, which lights the faces it shows; so the viewer's sun stands at 300 deg round and 45 deg up; the exposure from the building's luma: p10/p50/p90 172/174/176 at 0.5 against the photograph's 92/175/222 (204 at 0.7, 242 at the default 1.0; the model's faces are plain, so its spread is narrow)
